internal: two findings of the independent reviews of 2026-11-14 against the code view (crates/deep-diff-forge-graph/src/lexical.rs), each reproduced on the released v0.8.3 binary with a control before it was counted, and a third text found while the fix was written. (1) IR2-H-3, docs/reviews/claude-independent-review-2-20261114.md: Rust nests block comments, and the view ended one at the first */, so after /* /* */ a // cut the line and the call behind the last */ was hidden (src/net.rs: a fetch, a spawn, an unwrap, a todo after a nested comment that holds a quote, and an unwrap after a comment that holds //*; v0.8.3 reports no signal for the file, and process_spawn and network_fetch for its control). (2) IR4-H-1, docs/reviews/claude-independent-review-4-20261114.md: a character literal with an escape longer than one character put the view one quote out of step, so that '"' opened a string and "/*" a comment over the rest of the hunk (src/table.rs, a new file whose first line is such a constant: the unsafe block, the unwrap, the todo, the ignored test and the trivial assertion after it; src/escapes.rs, the same with '\u{1F600}'|'"' and a byte literal: v0.8.3 reports no evidence for either file, and unsafe_added for their controls). (3) src/piled.rs: a string and then a raw string that holds a comment opener on each of three lines; a scanner that counts comment depth has one reading for each depth, and the reading that resumed both strings, the compiler's, must not be the one dropped (found by the fuzz oracle against rustc's lexer while the fix was written; released versions read it right). Expected: every item. The fuzz target rust_code_view holds the view to the compiler's lexer for any text

internal: a fifth independent review by a Claude subagent (docs/reviews/claude-independent-review-5-20261114.md, IR5-H-1, IR5-M-1, IR5-M-2) and round 12 of Vesper's review (docs/reviews/vesper-v3-round12-report-20261114.md, VD3R12-M-1, VD3R12-M-2), 2026-11-14, each reproduced before it was counted. Expected: after a string over a line end, an unwrap, a todo, an ignored test and a trivial assertion with the comment /*""*/ between two of their tokens (src/union.rs), a conditional skip with a closing bracket inside a string of its condition (src/skip.rs), and the unwrap in a hunk of an existing file (src/cli.rs): the bytes of two readings were united and the union showed the comment's quotes between the tokens; raw identifiers after the left-to-right mark U+200E, which the compiler takes for white space (src/marks.rs); a spawn on a line added inside an existing block comment, // */ ... /*, and the same with the opener added by an earlier hunk (src/net.rs, src/lib.rs): a side below line 1 is also read as beginning inside a block comment; a spawn under a shebang line that holds /* (src/bin/tool.rs); every item under m!(k#r"\"); m!(" /* "); (src/kraw.rs), which rustc 1.99.1 reads as k, # and a raw string in editions 2015 and 2018 and refuses in 2021 and 2024; and the unwrap on the line that closes a string opened above the hunk (src/db.rs, the review's honest case): a side that, read from code, ends inside a string is also read as beginning inside one. Declared false positives, the cost of those two further readings: a call in the text of a string after **/ in a hunk below line 1 (src/glob.rs), and a call in the text of a string in a hunk that ends inside another string (src/log.rs). Declared misses: the ignored test and the trivial assertion under the same text (that release had no rule for them, and the reader of tokens reads the view of the newer editions); and a spawn after // "; in a hunk whose string was opened by an earlier hunk (src/store.rs): read from code that side carries nothing over a line end, so nothing says it began inside a string

internal: a sixth independent review by a Claude subagent (docs/reviews/claude-independent-review-6-20261114.md, IR6-H-1, IR6-H-2, IR6-H-3, IR6-L-1, IR6-L-4), round 13 of Vesper's review (docs/reviews/vesper-v3-round13-report-20261114.md, VD3R13-M-1) and the review of the port of the Rust scanner to the released line (LF-H-1), 2026-11-14, each reproduced before it was counted, with `git apply` 2.56.0 and rustc 1.99.1 where a claim is about them. Expected. The place of a hunk is where Git must put it: a spawn on a line added inside an existing block comment in a hunk whose header says +1 (src/placed.rs: Git applies it at line 9), the same with the comment opened by an earlier hunk (src/second.rs), and a line `#! ...` inside a macro call in a hunk that says +1 (src/macro.rs: no shebang, since the old position is 6). Hunks Git must put together are one text: a call cut in two by the hunks of a created file (src/split.rs) and by a hunk of added lines after one that ends its file (src/end.rs), a spawn after a comment two deep opened in the first hunk of a created file (src/deep.rs), and a spawn below a string opened in the first hunk whose text holds crates/*/*/Cargo.toml (src/glob.rs). A join is a further reading and takes none away: two hunks of added lines only, the first leaving a block comment open, the second a spawn and a call (src/zero.rs: plain `git apply` puts both at the end of the file, where the second is the text of that comment, and the hunks are also read as that one text; `git apply --unidiff-zero` puts each where its numbers say, where the comment is closed between them and rustc compiles the second as code, so each hunk is always read on its own as well; the first build of this round read the second only as a continuation and lost both items, which round 13 reported). A side that carries anything over a line end is also read from inside a string, and from inside a raw string: #[ignore] added between two tests whose expected output is a raw string over lines (tests/snapshots.rs, a `diff -U3`), a test removed between two strings (tests/t.rs), a spawn after the closing line of a string, on a line that holds the string "/*" (src/help.rs), a spawn after a raw string whose text ends in a backslash (src/paths.rs), and what release 0.8.3 reported and round 13 lost, a spawn and an unsafe block below a string whose text has more comment openers than closers (src/main.rs, src/script.rs, plain `git diff`s). And the general answer: a hunk that reaches the top of its file is read exactly, so the full-context forms of two declared misses are found (src/full/strcode.rs, src/full/nested.rs). A hunk with old position 1 is the top of its file whatever its new position says, and a line comment there is a line comment (src/top.rs: nothing is reported). Declared misses, each as a bare fragment: a spawn after a string that began above the hunk, on a line whose quotes balance (src/strcode.rs: read from code nothing is carried over a line end, so nothing says the side began in a string); a spawn two comments deep behind `// */ //` (src/nested.rs, src/depth2.rs: a side is read from inside one comment, not two); a call cut in two by two hunks that touch while the second header says they do not (src/apart.rs: Git finds a hunk by its context, wherever its header says it is); and four spellings of a suppressed lint that the one-line rule does not read (src/allow.rs: a comment inside the attribute, the attribute over two lines, `cfg_attr(all(), allow(...))`, `expect(...)`). Declared false positives, the cost of the further readings: a call in the text of a string on a line after a block comment that the hunk does not see the end of (src/notes.rs: the side carries a comment over a line end and is read from inside a string too), and the two items release 0.8.3 reported in the text of a string after a string over lines (src/legacy.rs: the reading of that release, by its own rules, is kept so that nothing it reports is lost; the two items of newer signals that the same text gave until round 13 are not reported). Since 2026-11-15 three of the declared misses above are found and expected: the call cut in two by hunks that touch while the second header says they do not (src/apart.rs: the first half ends on `x.unwrap`, and the edge of a side is read), and two of the four spellings of a suppressed lint (src/allow.rs: the comment inside the attribute and the attribute over two lines are the tokens `#`, `[`, `allow`, `(` to the reader; `cfg_attr(all(), allow(...))` and `expect(...)` stay declared). Since 0.11.0 (F2b) `#[expect(..)]` switches a lint off as `#[allow(..)]` does and is read by the same rules: line 8 of src/allow.rs is expected; and `cfg_attr(all(), allow(...))` (line 6), whose allowance the reading of a conditional attribute follows as it follows `ignore`. Corrected 2026-11-15 (seventh independent review, IR7-L-3): Git starts looking for a hunk at its NEW position and takes the nearest place that has its old lines, so the hunk of src/placed.rs goes to line 9 when its lines stand there and not at line 1; where this text says that Git places a hunk by its old position, only positions 0 and 1 are meant, which say the hunk must be at the beginning. The expectations did not change. Since round 16 (2026-11-15) the call of src/apart.rs is a declared miss again: `.unwrap` with nothing after it at the end of a side is no evidence by itself (a field can be named so), and neither number of the second hunk says the two touch Release 0.10.0 (ruling 1 of its integration): the parser refuses a hunk that plain `git apply` places elsewhere than its header says (no context past line 1, or after a hunk with no trailing context). The hunks of src/zero.rs that had no context carry a blank line of context, as Git writes context; their items are unchanged (measured against 0.9.0). The sections of src/deep.rs, src/end.rs, src/glob.rs, src/split.rs are creations in several hunks, hunks that touch, or read what only such hunks give; they moved with their expectations to fixtures/eval-refused-by-parser/.
